Article Title: 'Nobody can browbeat judiciary': SC issues notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others over October 12 march
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi , Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other protestors over their October 12 march to the apex court to protest alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The bench, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi, said issuing notice on the petition did not mean it was condoning the conduct of the political leaders during the march.ALSO READ: Imran Khan asked to leave India: What rights do OCI cardholders have? “We will issue notice but we want to know his conduct on the next date of hearing,” the CJI said, referring to Rahul.During the hearing, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, “We are not sitting in ivory towers, we are aware of statements made outside the Court” after lawyers referred to attempts to “browbeat” the judiciary through the march. The CJI said the court would ask Rahul to explain how crowds entered the Supreme Court premises during the demonstration.The INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli – March for Democracy’, led by Rahul, brought thousands of supporters into central Delhi on October 12. The opposition was demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR exercise over alleged electoral irregularities.The march saw supporters gather along roads between Connaught Place and the Supreme Court, waving party flags and raising slogans.Police stopped the procession near Barakhamba Road, where some demonstrators pushed through barricades as security personnel attempted to hold them back. The crowd later gathered along Bhagwan Das Road, with some supporters climbing onto parked police vehicles and buses.Rahul was joined by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Akhilesh Yadav, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav and other INDIA bloc leaders. The procession followed the CJI’s refusal to meet opposition representatives seeking to submit a memorandum on alleged electoral irregularities. He had advised them to file a formal petition, citing matters already pending before the court.The opposition’s separate petition challenging the SIR process alleges arbitrary voter deletions and seeks greater transparency and safeguards in the revision of electoral rolls. The Supreme Court also issued notice to the Election Commission of India on that plea.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and other protestors over their October 12 march to the apex court. The bench, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi, said issuing notice did not mean it was condoning the conduct of the political leaders.

Article Title: 'Don't try to bulldoze another Constitutional Amendment Bill': Kharge writes to PM Modi
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Friday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the delay in proroguing the Monsoon Session of Parliament, which ended in August, describing the situation as “unprecedented”.Urging PM Modi not to “bulldoze” another “far-reaching” Constitutional Amendment Bill, Kharge reiterated his demand for an all-party meeting to discuss the government’s proposals in detail before they are finalised for consideration in Parliament."It has already been 64 days since the Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 and both Houses of Parliament are yet to be prorogued. This scenario is unprecedented," Kharge said in his letter, which Congress MP Jairam Ramesh shared on X.The Rajya Sabha leader of opposition recalled writing to the prime minister on April 11, seeking an all-party meeting before the government introduced the Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation, which subsequently failed to pass in the Lok Sabha.“You may kindly recall that I had written to you on April 11 to convene an all-party meeting before bringing any Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation.You did not do so. Thereafter, you made the bills public on the late evening of April 14 and convened a special session on April 16. The Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation failed to muster the necessary two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17 by a decisive margin,” Kharge said.“Thereafter, on July 16 and August 27, I wrote to you again, reiterating our request for an all-party meeting. I am now making this request for the fourth time. All political parties must be given sufficient time to deliberate among themselves, with each other and with all other stakeholders. Please do not once again try to bulldoze a far-reaching Constitutional Amendment Bill through Parliament, as you attempted earlier, only for it to meet its well-deserved fate,” he added.The Monsoon Session of Parliament began on July 20 and concluded as scheduled on August 13. However, proceedings were repeatedly disrupted over issues including the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, the NEET paper leak and allegations of police excesses against NEET protesters in Delhi.
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the delay in proroguing the Monsoon Session of Parliament. Urging PM Modi not to “bulldoze” another “far-reaching” Constitutional Amendment Bill, Kharge reiterated his demand for an all-party meeting.

Article Title: ‘Why is govt scared?’ Congress’s Vijay Wadettiwar slams Centre over delimitation, delay in all-party meet
Article Text:
He stressed that matters of national importance should be discussed with both the ruling alliance and the Opposition

Kharge flags 64-day delay in proroguing Parliament

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar on Saturday accused the Centre of acting arbitrarily over the proposed delimitation exercise, questioning why the government was reluctant to convene an all-party meeting on the issue.His remarks came a day after Congress president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the fourth time, demanding an all-party meeting to discuss the delimitation proposals before they are finalised and introduced in Parliament.“Modi Govt is acting arbitrarily. They did not even get the majority; they formed the Govt with support of other parties. Opposition is strong. But irrespective of the Opposition being strong or small, such matters should be discussed by both sides...Why is the Govt scared? Because they have done wrong. So, they won't convene (an all-party meeting) and discuss...” Wadettiwar said.He stressed that matters of national importance should be discussed with both the ruling alliance and the Opposition, irrespective of the latter's strength.In his letter to Modi on Friday, Kharge raised procedural and constitutional concerns over the status of Parliament's Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but had not been formally prorogued.“It has already been 64 days since the Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13, 2026 and both Houses of Parliament are yet to be prorogued. This scenario is unprecedented,” Kharge wrote.Adjournment sine die suspends parliamentary proceedings indefinitely without specifying a date for the next sitting. Prorogation, by contrast, formally ends a session through an order issued by the President of India.Kharge argued that the prolonged delay in proroguing both Houses had fuelled speculation about a possible sudden reconvening of Parliament or an extension of the session, potentially bypassing the standard notice periods for lawmakers.Kharge urged the Centre to clarify the status of the Monsoon Session and convene an all-party meeting before introducing any new delimitation proposals.The Congress has also called for political parties and regional stakeholders to be given sufficient time to examine draft legislation before it is brought to Parliament.That shift from constitutional mandate to parliamentary choice was the provision that most alarmed critics.
Article Summary: Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar accused the Centre of acting arbitrarily over the proposed delimitation exercise. He questioned why the government was reluctant to convene an all-party meeting on the issue. His remarks came a day after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Article Title: ‘Opposition’s duty is to oppose, expose, depose’: Congress defends ‘regime change’ remark
Article Text:
‘Regime change normal in democracy’: Chidambaram hits back at BJP

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader and former Union minister P Chidambaram on Saturday defended the use of the phrase “regime change” in a democracy, amid a political row over remarks by student activist Neha Bora and senior advocate Prashant Bhushan during protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In a post on X, Chidambaram questioned the BJP's reaction to the phrase and said the Opposition's duty was to “oppose, expose and depose” the government.“Why is the BJP apoplectic with feigned rage on the use of the phrase 'regime change'? 'Regime change' is normal in a democracy. The duty of the Opposition is to 'oppose, expose and depose' the government Which means: oppose in politics, expose in Parliament and depose through elections,” he wrote.The controversy erupted after Bhushan described the ongoing agitation against Gyanesh Kumar as a “fight for regime change”, while Bora referred to the Gen Z movement in Bangladesh.The BJP interpreted the remarks as evidence of an attempt to remove the Narendra Modi government outside the electoral process, an allegation rejected by the Opposition. The Congress has maintained that peaceful protests against an elected government and efforts to replace it through elections are legitimate democratic activities.The BJP, however, has argued that references to Bangladesh and the language used by some protest organisers point to a broader attempt to create political unrest.Several BJP leaders criticised the opposition over the remarks, including Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, party president Nitin Nabin, Uttar Pradesh BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary, Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi, Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. BJP spokespersons Pradeep Bhandari and Sambit Patra also joined the criticism.The row has unfolded amid protests against Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the electoral process.
Article Summary: P Chidambaram says Opposition's duty is to ‘oppose, expose and depose’ the government. The controversy erupted after Bhushan described the ongoing agitation as a ‘fight for regime change’ The BJP interpreted the remarks as evidence of an attempt to remove the Narendra Modi government outside the electoral process.

Article Title: ‘Police can break bones, not satyagraha’: Rahul Gandhi alleges Delhi Police refused to file FIR over assault on student protesters
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday alleged that Delhi Police was refusing to register an FIR over the alleged assault on student protesters, claiming that two young women, Athira from Kerala and Ritu from Rajasthan, were among those beaten by the police.In a post on X, the Congress leader said he had spoken to Kerala home minister Ramesh Chennithala and Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president Govind Singh Dotasra over the incident.He added that a Zero FIR had already been registered in Kerala and said the Congress would pursue legal action against the officers concerned.“Two young women, Athira from Kerala and Ritu from Rajasthan, along with many others, were beaten by Delhi Police. I have spoken to Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala and Rajasthan PCC President Govind Singh Dotasra. A Zero FIR has already been registered in Kerala. We will pursue every legal route against the officers responsible, in Kerala, in Rajasthan and in the courts,” Rahul wrote.“Brutality by Amit Shah ’s Delhi Police will not go unchecked,” he added.Referring to the 1930 Dharasana Satyagraha, the Raebareli MP recalled how Sarojini Naidu had led unarmed satyagrahis into police lathis without retaliating.“Police can break bones. They cannot break a satyagraha,” he said.Former Congress president also described India’s youth, particularly young women, as fearless, determined and united in their efforts to defend democracy, adding that he stood with them.“India's youth, especially young women, are fearless, determined and united. They are standing up for our democracy, and I stand with them,” he wrote.Earlier on Wednesday, Rahul had accused Delhi Police of assaulting student protesters and warned the Centre against suppressing their voices amid demonstrations against the revision of electoral rolls.Addressing protesters in Delhi, he said the demonstration represented a collective voice that transcended religion, caste and gender. He urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah not to stand against the protesters.“As I said in my press conference, this is India. Amit Shah ji, take a good look at this. There is no Hindu here, no Muslim, no one of any specific caste; there is no woman, no man. There is one voice, one protest. It is the voice of India, and you are standing against this voice—the Prime Minister is standing against this voice. I suggest to you: do not stand against this voice. No one can stand against this voice,” Rahul had said.He also urged student protesters to document alleged police misconduct, saying the evidence would be used to seek accountability.Meanwhile, Delhi Police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke and All India Students' Association (AISA) chief Neha Bohra on Friday as they were heading to Connaught Place for the proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest.Dipke was detained while leaving his residence in Jhandewalan, while Bohra was picked up in Mandi House.Police informed Dipke that he was being placed under preventive detention, citing restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the Connaught Place area. He was also served notices referring to the restrictions and a previous undertaking to maintain public peace.Police had warned that the proposed rally could violate the restrictions if held without permission from the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC).Dipke was told that waving the national flag was not unlawful, but holding an unpermitted march and gathering a crowd could invite legal action.The detentions came amid heightened security arrangements in the national capital ahead of the proposed protest. Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar had earlier reviewed security arrangements with senior officers, while traffic police issued an advisory warning of possible disruption around Connaught Place.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi says two young women, Athira from Kerala and Ritu from Rajasthan, along with many others, were beaten by Delhi Police. Delhi Police detain Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke and All India Students' Association (AISA) chief Neha Bohra.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Friday accused the BJP of hypocrisy over its objections to calls for “regime change”, arguing that the Opposition’s stated goal was to defeat the government through elections.Speaking at a press conference titled “Albert Pinto Ko Gussa Kyoon Aata Hai”, Khera spoke on defence minister Rajnath Singh’s remarks against the opposition wanting a regime change.“We are we reiterating our objective… we have to defeat this government and change this system. So why has Rajnath Singh ji turned into Jagga Jasoos? Sherlock Holmes,” Khera said, referring to the defence minister’s allegations that the Congress and its allies were using youth-led protests against the Election Commission to fuel political unrest, alleging that they were seeking regime change in India along the lines of BangladeshKhera argued that changing a government through elections was a normal part of democracy and cited the 1977 change of government as an example. “Changing the regime through elections is precisely the Opposition’s goal, what else would our purpose be?” he said, accusing the BJP of having “lost the habit of practising democracy”.The Congress leader also defended the right to protest of people holding OCI cards, referring to controversy surrounding Imran Khan’s alleged plans to organise a protest in India.ALSO READ: 'Bangladesh-style regime change' bid: Rajnath slams opposition over Delhi protests “You praise the diaspora for celebrating Dandiya abroad but question Imran Khan’s right to protest in India because he’s an OCI,” Khera said.He accused the BJP of celebrating the Indian diaspora when it promoted Indian culture overseas but branding members of the same community as traitors when they criticised the government in India.Khera also referred to the controversy surrounding activist Prashant Bhushan’s remarks on regime change, saying Bhushan had been treated as a friend when he made similar demands in 2013 but was now being portrayed as an enemy.He also criticised what he described as the labelling of voices such as Bhojpuri singer Neha Singh Rathore as “leftist”, “urban Naxal” or “feminist”, and said the government should respond to criticism rather than attack its critics.
Article Summary: Congress leader Pawan Khera accuses the BJP of hypocrisy over its objections to calls for'regime change' He argues that the Opposition’s stated goal is to defeat the government through elections. “We are we reiterating our objective… we have to defeat this government and change this system. So why has Rajnath Singh ji turned into Jagga Jasoos? Sherlock Holmes,” he said.

Article Title: 'Entire movement orchestrated at Elon Musk's behest': Brij Bhushan Singh on CJP's Tiranga march
Article Text:

CJP protests arrests of leaders

NEW DELHI: BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on Friday alleged that Elon Musk was orchestrating the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest, calling it a conspiracy against India as the party prepared to hold demonstrations in Delhi and Mumbai.“This entire movement is being orchestrated at his (Elon Musk) behest. It is a massive conspiracy against our nation,” Singh said in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh. He alleged that India was being compared with Bangladesh and Pakistan and claimed the march was intended to intimidate the Supreme Court. Singh did not provide evidence for the allegations.The CJP has called for a flag march at Central Park in Delhi’s Connaught Place at 5pm on Friday, October 16, while its Mumbai unit has received police permission to hold a demonstration at Azad Maidan from 10am to 5pm.The proposed demonstrations follow the arrests of CJP co-conveners Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das after they reached Jantar Mantar in Delhi. The two were subsequently remanded to five days of judicial custody by a special executive magistrate.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has urged citizens to join the Delhi march, maintaining that waving the national flag is a democratic right. The party has also called for parallel Tiranga marches in other cities.In Mumbai, CJP in-charge Pranay Ahire said the demonstration was intended to assert the party’s patriotism.“We want to show the government that we are the real patriots, not the fake patriots or fake deshbhakts that this government is,” Ahire said in an Instagram video.Ahire said the party had permission for only a one-day protest and ruled out confirming any indefinite sit-in.Police sources said several companies of paramilitary forces would be deployed in and around Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar ahead of the proposed Delhi gathering. Barricades are expected at strategic locations, with police regulating the movement of protesters and commuters.A senior police officer said Connaught Place is not a designated protest site. Jantar Mantar has also been denotified as a designated protest site, the officer said, adding that demonstrations can be held at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the required permission.
Article Summary: CJP has called for a flag march at Central Park in Delhi’s Connaught Place at 5pm on Friday, October 16. Its Mumbai unit has received police permission to hold a demonstration at Azad Maidan from 10am to 5pm. The proposed demonstrations follow the arrests of CJP co-conveners Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: ‘Stop protecting the VIP’: Ankita Bhandari's parents detained after overnight protest over governor appointment
Article Text:
Congress backs parents as Delhi Police break up overnight dharna

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

After an overnight vigil at India Gate, a pre-dawn swoop by Delhi Police brought the dharna for “Justice to Ankita Bhandari” to an end. The cops arrived at the protest site at 4 am and took away the wailing parents of Ankita Bhandari, who was murdered in Uttarakhand in 2022.Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and, later, AICC general secretary KC Venugopal visited the protest site on Wednesday evening to express solidarity with the parents. After they left, scores of Congress MPs, MLAs and workers of the Youth Congress and NSUI, among others, joined the dharna. Uttarakhand MLA and Congress office-bearer Qazi Nizamuddin, MPs Pawan Khera, Jothi Mani and Imran Pratapgarhi, Congress spokespersons Supriya Shrinate, Gurdeep Sappal and Ragini Nayak, Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib, NSUI president Vinod Jakhar and Mahila Congress president Alka Lamba, among others, joined the vigil, which continued until early morning before being disrupted by the cops.Videos of the police action went viral, with Chib, Jakhar and others even trying to intercept the bus carrying the detainees.Ankita’s parents arrived from Uttarakhand on Wednesday evening and sat on a dharna along with activist Yogita Bhayana, holding a placard that read, “Stop protecting the VIP”. The continuing controversy over Ankita’s murder received a fresh lease of life with the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Gautam as governor.The controversy revolves around the “VIP” who had allegedly sought “special service” at the infamous resort then owned by the son of a BJP leader. Ankita resisted the pressure. Her body was found in a canal in 2022, leading to a murder case.In a social media post, the Congress said there were allegations that Gautam was the “VIP” in question. “Narendra Modi has rewarded Gautam with the governorship of Sikkim. The girls and women of the country are watching how Modi and his govt are protecting Gautam.Instead of giving them justice, the entire BJP govt is hellbent on suppressing the voice of Ankita’s parents,” it said.Ankita’s father urged the President of India to put Gautam’s appointment as governor on hold until the CBI inquiry into the issue is completed.Ankita’s parents were taken by the cops to Tilak Marg police station, where they were swiftly joined by Congress leaders protesting the police action against the parents, who were seeking justice for their deceased daughter.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and AICC general secretary KC Venugopal visited the protest site on Wednesday evening. Scores of Congress MPs, MLAs and workers of the Youth Congress and NSUI, among others, joined the dharna.

Article Title: 1 dead, 5 injured after DTC bus hits scooter in Delhi’s Anand Parbat
Article Text:
DTC bus rams into a scooter and many others in Anand Parbat area

(With Agency Inputs)





NEW DELHI: At least one person was killed and five others injured after a Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) bus hit a scooter in the Anand Parbat area on Saturday, police sources said.According to preliminary information, the accident took place in the DBG Road area.Both men riding the scooter sustained serious injuries and were rushed to a hospital, where one of them was declared dead, the sources said.The bus went out of control after hitting the scooter, injuring at least four other people, they added.
Article Summary: A Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) bus hit a scooter in the Anand Parbat area on Saturday. Both men riding the scooter sustained serious injuries and were rushed to a hospital, where one of them was declared dead. At least four other people were injured in the accident.

Article Title: Nanded man wanted in intercaste marriage murder case held from Bhopal Central Prison
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A 29-year-old man wanted in a murder case registered by Nanded Rural police in Sept 2024 was arrested from Bhopal Central Jail in Madhya Pradesh on Thursday, where he was allegedly lodged under a false identity in connection with another case.Police said the accused, identified as Palwinder Singh Lachmansingh Chavan, was produced before a Nanded court on Thursday and remanded to police custody till Oct 17.Investigators said Chavan had been absconding since the murder of Shivam Suraj Gaikwad on Sept 20, 2024. Acting on a tip-off, a Nanded police team led by sub-inspector Ravindra Taru verified his presence in Bhopal Central Jail, secured a production warrant and brought him to Nanded.Nanded superintendent of police Neelabh Rohan said the arrest was made as part of a special drive to trace absconding accused involved in serious crimes across the district.Police said Gaikwad was allegedly murdered over his intercaste marriage. As per a complaint filed by his brother, Karan Gaikwad, Chavan and another accused had allegedly threatened Shivam over the marriage. Chavan is accused of attacking Shivam with a sword, causing fatal head and neck injuries.The accused allegedly dumped the body in Godavari river to destroy evidence.Police registered a case under sections 103(1), 238 and 3(5) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with relevant provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. “The co-accused, Devansh alias Devansingh Karansingh Sikkarwar, was arrested and a chargesheet was filed against him in Dec 2024,” an officer said.During the investigation, police found that Chavan had allegedly been using the identity of Balkar Singh, son of Lakshman Singh, while in custody in a govt railway police case registered in Bhopal in 2026.
Article Summary: Palwinder Singh Lachmansingh Chavan was arrested from Bhopal Central Jail. He was allegedly lodged under a false identity in connection with another case. Chavan had been absconding since the murder of Shivam Suraj Gaikwad on Sept 20, 2024.

Article Title: Sule alleges ‘vote chori’, seeks poll reforms; questions govt’s farmer aid promise
Article Text:
Supriya Sule

Kolhapur

:

Independent candidate claims Sena support





NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule on Friday alleged large-scale manipulation of voter lists and called for electoral reforms to ensure fairness and a level playing field in elections.“In cooperative elections, voter lists are prepared months in advance. In general elections, however, the process remains open till the last moment. While political parties are busy campaigning, names are allegedly being added to and deleted from voter lists,” she said while addressing a press conference in Kolhapur while campaigning for Congress and NCP (SP) candidates in the Pune graduates’ and teachers’ constituency elections.Sule compared alleged electoral malpractice to clearing an examination through copying. “Don’t pass an exam by copying. Today, many people feel that ‘vote chori’ has taken place on a large scale. That is why a massive number of people turned up when an opposition delegation approached Supreme Court with a petition,” she said.The MP also targeted Centre over the economy, claiming that govt was being forced to sell profitable public sector undertakings. Referring to the proposed disinvestment of IDBI Bank, she alleged that the economy was under severe stress.“The reality is that the economy has slowed significantly. RBI reserves have been used on an unprecedented scale to stabilise the dollar, while food inflation continues to soar,” she said.Sule also questioned chief minister Devendra Fadnavis ’s reported assurance of providing Rs 5,000 to farmers for Diwali. She sought clarity on whether the proposed assistance would be over and above pending instalments under the Namo Shetkari Yojana. “Pay the pending dues separately and provide the Rs 5,000 separately. Farmers should not be misled,” she said, while reiterating her demand for compensation of Rs 1 lakh per hectare for drought-hit farmers.Independent candidate Sachin Sanap, contesting from Pune teachers’ constituency, claimed in Kolhapur that Shiv Sena workers and members were campaigning for him despite deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde’s backing for the BJP candidate.Sanap, a former officer on special duty to minister and Sena leader Uday Samant, remained in the fray after refusing to withdraw his candidature. The party’s official nominee, Mangesh Chivate, withdrew from the contest at the last moment.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule alleged large-scale manipulation of voter lists. She was campaigning for Congress and NCP candidates in the Pune graduates’ and teachers’ constituency elections. Sule compared alleged electoral malpractice to clearing an examination through copying.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Ulhasnagar social activist Haresh Gajwani shot dead outside railway station, 3 arrested
Article Text:
Haresh Gajwani was murdered outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night.





ULHASNAGAR: Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of social worker Haresh Gajwani, who was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan.According to preliminary investigations, Gajwani and Naidu had a long-standing dispute. In 2021, counter-cases were registered against the two sides following a dispute, which allegedly contributed to continuing tensions between Gajwani and the accused.Police said the three suspects were traced and detained with the help of CCTV footage. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives behind the murder.Gajwani, 54, was allegedly attacked by three assailants who fired two rounds at him before fleeing the scene. Locals and police took him to Central Hospital, where doctors declared him "brought dead".Recently, Gajwani had posted on X, tagging senior officials from various police departments, as well as the chief minister, deputy chief minister and FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. In his posts, he had highlighted alleged illegal activities in the area and claimed that some police personnel were supporting those involved. He had also expressed fears for his life, warning that the police personnel he had accused would also be responsible if anything happened to him.
Article Summary: Haresh Gajwani, 54, was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday. Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Mahayuti infighting intensifies over MLC polls amid growing farmer anger over drought
Article Text:
Farmers said politicians are more interested in politics than in addressing the real issue of drought

Pune





: Amid the drought crisis, one-upmanship is playing out among Mahayuti partners— BJP Shiv Sena , and NCP— in the run-up to the teachers’ and graduates’ constituency polls. Farmer activists have vented their anger at the ruling alliance for prioritising election campaigning over providing much-needed drought relief to growers.They have demanded that the govt release financial aid immediately. Jayaji Suryavanshi, a farmer activist from Marathwada region, added, “By now, aid should have reached farmers, but it is unfortunate that politicians are busy bickering. They must rise above politics and proactively help the farming community before the situation deteriorates further.”Although senior leaders of the Mahayuti alliance claim they will fight the teachers’ and graduates’ constituency polls unitedly, a severe lack of coordination is evident. Several rebel candidates have filed nominations, posing a direct challenge to the alliance’s official picks. A day after deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde claimed during his Pune visit that Shiv Sena would campaign for BJP’s candidate, Kaustubh Gawade, for the teachers’ constituency, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis announced that his party would instead support rebel candidate Sachin Sanap against Gawade.A similar tussle is unfolding between BJP and Shiv Sena for Amravati seat. Despite the chief minister’s party nominating its official candidate, Kiran Sarnaik, BJP rebel Dilip Kadu has thrown his hat into the ring. In Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Shiv Sena and NCP are at loggerheads; Sena has threatened to withhold support from its ally even though the seat was officially allocated to NCP.Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana founder Raju Shetti said, “While the drought situation is getting worse, nobody should be talking about elections.The sole focus of the govt should be extending a helping hand to farmers. Unfortunately, that is not happening. Politicians are more interested in politics than in addressing the real issue of drought.”Maharashtra Legislative Council (MLC) polls for five seats in the graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies will be held on Oct 23. Among these five seats, BJP is contesting graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies in Pune division, as well as graduates’ constituency in Nagpur division. Meanwhile, Shiv Sena is contesting Amravati teachers’ constituency, and NCP has fielded its candidate for Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar graduates’ constituency.
Article Summary: Farmer activists have vented their anger at the ruling alliance for prioritising election campaigning over providing much-needed drought relief to growers. Senior leaders of the Mahayuti alliance claim they will fight the teachers’ and graduates’ constituency polls unitedly. Several rebel candidates have filed nominations, posing a direct challenge to the alliance’s official picks.

Article Title: Contractor, Tonner Supplier Charged for Negligence in Godhani Chlorine Leak
Article Text:
File photo

Nagpur:





More than 50 days after a chlorine leak at the Godhani water treatment plant led to the hospitalisation of over 50 people, Mankapur police have registered a case of negligence against the contractor and the chlorine tonner supplier. Maharashtra Jeevan Pradhikaran (MJP) officials lodged the complaint on the district collector’s directions.The charges relate to negligent handling of a poisonous substance (chlorine gas), acts endangering lives and causing hurt, and public nuisance following a leak from a standby 900kg chlorine tonner around midnight on August 24.District collector Kumar Ashirwad had ordered an inquiry into the incident and directed MJP officials to initiate criminal proceedings against those responsible.The contractor was responsible for maintaining the tonners and the plant, as well as ensuring adequate safety measures.Mankapur police station senior inspector Haresh Kalsekar said prima facie negligence had led to the leak. “Even after the leak took place, there were no proper arrangements at the site to prevent the gas from creating havoc or to control the damage,” he said.The probe revealed missing gas sensors and alarms, the absence of a proper neutralisation system, inadequate protective equipment, no clear emergency plan, and the tonner being kept in the open.“Some MJP officials may also come under the scanner. We will summon the accused and the concerned persons for questioning, and aim to file a strong chargesheet at the earliest,” Kalsekar said.
Article Summary: A chlorine leak at the Godhani water treatment plant led to the hospitalisation of over 50 people. Mankapur police have registered a case of negligence against the contractor and the chlorine tonner supplier. The charges relate to negligent handling of a poisonous substance (chlorine gas)

Article Title: Cyber fraudsters pose as CBI officers, digitally arrest 75-year-old
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Cyber fraudsters posing as CBI officers duped a 75-year-old man of Rs8 lakh through a digital arrest scam by threatening him with arrest in a fake sex racket case. Beltarodi police have registered a case against unidentified accused.According to the police, the complainant, a resident of New Manish Nagar, received a call from an unidentified person who claimed to be a CBI officer. The caller allegedly accused him of being involved in a sex racket and threatened that he would be arrested.The fraudsters used intimidation to keep the senior citizen under digital surveillance, making him believe that he was under house arrest. Later, other fraudsters joined the call and threatened him with legal action.The accused allegedly forced the victim to transfer Rs8 lakh from his account. The transactions were carried out online. Realising that he had been cheated, the victim approached Beltarodi police and lodged a complaint on Oct 15.Police registered a case under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita dealing with cheating and fraud, along with provisions of the Information Technology Act.
Article Summary: Cyber fraudsters posing as CBI officers duped a 75-year-old man of Rs8 lakh. The fraudsters used intimidation to keep the senior citizen under digital surveillance, making him believe that he was under house arrest. Beltarodi police have registered a case against unidentified accused.

Article Title: Woman cheated of Rs22 lakh, one arrested
Article Text:
Nashik

:





The Ambad police have arrested Vinod Daund, 35, a resident of Chehedi, Nashik Road, in connection with an alleged Rs 22.22 lakh cheating case involving a 55-year-old flower seller and two other suspects.According to the police, Daund and a couple allegedly cheated the woman, a resident of Kamodnagar, Indiranagar, between Jan 1, 2022, and July 1, 2026.In her complaint, the woman stated that the trio had promised to arrange a Rs 1.2 crore loan for her from a Chennai-based finance company. They also assured her of high interest returns on investments in the company.The woman allegedly paid Rs 2.8 lakh to get the loan approved and invested another Rs 11 lakh. The suspects also took jewellery worth Rs 7 lakh, another Rs 1 lakh in cash and a cellphone worth Rs 22,000 purchased in her name.She later discovered that the loan had not been sanctioned and that she was not receiving the promised returns. Realising she had been cheated, she approached the Ambad police, who registered a case and arrested Daund. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: The Ambad police have arrested Vinod Daund, 35, in connection with an alleged Rs 22.22 lakh cheating case involving a 55-year-old flower seller and two other suspects. Daund and a couple allegedly cheated the woman between Jan 1, 2022, and July 1, 2026.

Article Title: Hunt on for man accused of sexual assault of 15-year-old in Puducherry
Article Text:
Chennai:





Royapuram all-women police have registered a case under the Pocso Act against a photographer accused of sexually assaulting a 15-year-old girl at a hotel in Puducherry in Aug.Police registered a zero FIR and transferred it to Puducherry for investigation. A zero FIR allows police to register a case regardless of where the crime occurred and transfer it to the police station with jurisdiction. A team from the Union territory arrived in Chennai on Friday to question and apprehend the accused, Thiagu, but could not find him in Royapuram.Police said Chennai district Child Welfare Committee got information about the alleged abuse in Sept, and after speaking to the girl, filed a police complaint.According to the complaint, the girl’s mother, who knew Thiagu for 14 years, had agreed to let him marry her daughter after she turned 18. The girl had dropped out of school after Class IX.The girl, her mother and Thiagu reportedly travelled to Puducherry on Aug 28 for a photo shoot and stayed at a hotel near Muthialpet. Thiagu allegedly sexually assaulted the girl on Aug 30 while her mother was outside the room.Police said they were searching for Thiagu.
Article Summary: Police registered a zero FIR and transferred it to Puducherry for investigation. A zero FIR allows police to register a case regardless of where the crime occurred and transfer it to the police station with jurisdiction. A team from the Union territory arrived in Chennai on Friday to question and apprehend the accused, Thiagu.

Article Title: Vijay’s visit to Thrissur cancelled due to heavy rain in Coimbatore
Article Text:
CM Vijay





COIMBATORE: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay ’s planned visit to Kerala was cancelled on Friday due to heavy rain and adverse weather conditions in Coimbatore.Vijay was scheduled to travel by helicopter to Thrissur in Kerala after inaugurating the Periyar Arivulagam Library and Science Centre in Coimbatore. He was expected to attend a Navaratri celebration at the residence of a prominent jewellery businessman in Kerala.Two helicopters were stationed at the temporary helipads on the Police Recruitment School ground for the trip. However, the weather disrupted the planned journey, leading to its cancellation. Vijay later left for Chennai.
Article Summary: Vijay was scheduled to travel by helicopter to Thrissur in Kerala after inaugurating the Periyar Arivulagam Library and Science Centre in Coimbatore. He was expected to attend a Navaratri celebration at the residence of a prominent jewellery businessman.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Temple gold theft: Staffer, friend arrested for stealing jewellery
Article Text:
Temple gold theft: Staffer, friend arrested for stealing jewellery

Dindigul

:





A temporary woman employee at the Palani Idumban temple’s devasthanam office in Sivagiripatti and her male friend were arrested for stealing and selling 20 sovereigns of gold jewellery and 3kg of silver articles belonging to the temple.Police identified the accused as Niranjana of Pappampatti and her friend Prabakaran of Neykkarappatti.According to police, during an audit conducted after executive officer (in charge) Narasimman assumed charge a few months ago, officials found that several gold ornaments and silver articles kept in a bureau at the temple office were missing. On May 30, he filed a case of stolen jewellery with the Palani Town police.During the investigation, police discovered that Niranjana had been stealing temple ornaments in small quantities over a period of time. She was then selling the stolen items with the help of Prabakaran.Following their arrest, police recovered all the stolen items.
Article Summary: A temporary employee at the Palani devasthanam office in Sivagiripatti and her male friend were arrested for stealing and selling 20 sovereigns of gold jewellery and 3kg of silver articles. Police identified the accused as Niranjana and her friend Prabakaran of Neykkarappatti.

Article Title: Chennai techie held for death threats to CM on Instagram
Article Text:
Chennai techie held for death threats to CM on Instagram





Madurai: A 25-year-old IT professional from Kanchipuram was arrested on charges of posting death threats and abusive comments against chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Instagram . The accused used VPN services and public Wi-Fi networks to conceal his identity while uploading more than 1,500 posts through a fake account.Police said Prakash worked at an IT firm in Chennai. He frequently targeted the chief minister in the comment sections of news channels' Instagram pages. He posted one such threat on Sept 28 when Vijay visited Madurai to launch the Thaai Maaman Thangam Mothiram scheme. Subsequently, city cybercrime police registered a case on Sept 29.Police inspector T Babu told TOI that Prakash took several precautions to avoid detection. Apart from using virtual private network (VPN) services to mask his IP address, he accessed the internet through public Wi-Fi networks and avoided using his personal mobile phone. "We traced the origin IP address used to create the fake Instagram account. Although he used a VPN, we obtained details through an alternative mobile number linked to the profile," Babu said.Prakash was produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody on Wednesday. City police commissioner S Rajendiran monitored the investigation that led to the arrest.
Article Summary: 25-year-old IT professional from Kanchipuram was arrested on charges of posting death threats and abusive comments against chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Instagram. The accused used VPN services and public Wi-Fi networks to conceal his identity while uploading more than 1,500 posts.

Article Title: CM urges Jaishankar to take up fishers’ arrest with Maldives
Article Text:
CM urges Jaishankar to take up fishers’ arrest with Maldives





Madurai: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay has written to external affairs minister S Jaishankar seeking his intervention to secure the release of 25 fishermen from Tuticorin district who were arrested by Maldives Coast Guard.In his letter, Vijay said the fishermen along with three mechanised fishing boats were detained by Maldives Coast Guard in the early hours of Oct 13. He requested the external affairs minister to take up the matter with the Government of Maldives through appropriate diplomatic channels and facilitate early release and safe repatriation of the fishermen and their boats.
Article Summary: C Joseph Vijay has written to external affairs minister S Jaishankar seeking his intervention to secure the release of 25 fishermen from Tuticorin district. Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: Nedumbassery car crash: Decide on replies of two bar hotels in seven days, Kerala HC tells excise commissioner
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court has directed the excise commissioner to decide within seven days on the replies submitted by two bar hotels in Kochi to show-cause notices issued for allegedly serving liquor to a 19-year-old man accused in the Nedumbassery car crash case, in which three youngsters were killed.A bench of Justice M A Abdul Hakhim issued the order while disposing of petitions filed by Polakulath Tourist Home in Vyttila and Monsoon Empress on the Palarivattom Bypass, challenging the suspension of their bar licences and the show-cause notices issued to them.The petitioners submitted that cases had been registered against both hotels under Section 56(b) of the Abkari Act for allegedly serving liquor to Suhail, a person under the age of 23 years, who allegedly drove the vehicle. Subsequently, their bar licences were suspended and show-cause notices were issued asking why their licences should not be cancelled.The petitioners submitted replies to the notices and later approached the court, challenging the excise commissioner’s actions on the ground that the decisions had been taken without hearing them. During the hearing, counsel for the petitioners sought a directive to the commissioner to consider their replies. Accordingly, the bench disposed of the petitions, directing the commissioner to decide on the replies within seven days.
Article Summary: The high court has directed the excise commissioner to decide within seven days on the replies submitted by two bar hotels in Kochi to show-cause notices issued to them. A bench of Justice M A Abdul Hakhim issued the order while disposing of petitions filed by Polakulath Tourist Home in Vyttila and Monsoon Empress on the Palarivattom Bypass.

Article Title: Appoint special public prosecutors exclusively for Pocso cases within six weeks, Kerala HC tells govt
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court has directed the state govt to appoint special public prosecutors exclusively for Pocso cases within six weeks.The bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar was considering a PIL filed by the district court bar association, Thodupuzha-Muttom, challenging a govt order that allows special public prosecutors appointed for Pocso cases to handle non-Pocso cases filed under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. Despite the state govt justifying the decision by arguing that no law bars such an arrangement, the bench rejected the argument, referring to a 2020 Supreme Court order in a suo motu case.In the order, the apex court emphasised the need to appoint special public prosecutors exclusively to conduct Pocso cases. It also observed that the job assigned to public prosecutors handling Pocso cases is onerous and must be carried out with great care and sensitivity. Hence, there is a need not only to appoint exclusive public prosecutors but also to develop a training programme to equip them to deal with issues that may arise in their courts.Referring to the decision, the HC division bench held that the impugned govt order permitting special public prosecutors appointed for Pocso cases to conduct non-Pocso cases could not be sustained. The bench also directed the state govt to consider establishing the remaining 13 permanent, exclusive Pocso special courts, one in each district except Ernakulam, in compliance with the apex court’s directions.The decision in this regard shall be communicated to the high court administration within four weeks.Additionally, the bench directed the registrar (district judiciary) to ensure that all Pocso courts conform to the provisions of the Pocso Act . If any existing Pocso court does not comply with any of the prescribed requirements, immediate steps shall be taken to make the necessary additions and alterations to ensure compliance with the Pocso Act and the guidelines under the JJ Act, the bench added.
Article Summary: The high court has directed the state govt to appoint special public prosecutors exclusively for Pocso cases within six weeks. The bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar was considering a PIL filed by the district court bar association.
